newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED FACE HARD TEST AGAINST BOGEY TEAM CHELSEA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-UNITED FACE HARD TEST AGAINST BOGEY TEAM CHELSEA.

text.p: If Manchester United had to play Chelsea every week the championship trophy would not be going back to Old Trafford.
In the last four years as United have claimed three league titles they have had constant trouble with the Stamford Bridge men.

Earlier this season Chelsea won 2-1 at Old Trafford with goals by Michael Duberry and Gianluca Vialli and it should not have been seen as a surprise - the Londoners have lost there just twice in 22 years.
In United's dazzling 1993-94 season they lost just four league games - two of them to Chelsea - and the league leaders will go to London on Saturday knowing they are in for a fight.
However, the men who scored the goals for the Blues earlier in the season are unlikely to be starting this time.
Centre back Duberry has not played since January 11 while Vialli is being kept on the bench by the success of the Gianfranco Zola/Mark Hughes partnership.
"It's the first time in my career that I haven't played in the first team," the former Sampdoria and Italy star told 90 Minutes magazine.
"I've just got to wait my time, train hard and do my best to change the mind of my manager."

He did get a start and scored twice in Chelsea's most dramatic performance of the season - the 4-2 defeat of Liverpool in the F.A. Cup - but it was only after the introduction of Hughes that the Blues turned round a 2-0 deficit.
Coach Ruud Gullit is delighted with the combination of Hughes' brawn and Zola's artistry. Vialli's style falls somewhere between the two and he again looks a likely substitute for Saturday.
Chelsea played a friendly in Italy against AC Milan on Wednesday, losing 2-0, but Gullit made eight changes at half time to give the youngsters in the squad some European experience.
At the same time Manchester United were involved in a bruising premier league encounter with Arsenal.
The champions emerged with three points from a hugely important 2-1 win - but also with injury worries.
Midfielder Nicky Butt aggravated an ankle injury that had had kept him out of the previous seven games and looks set to be out for another two weeks.
"That's a major blow for us," said manager Alex Ferguson. "It's a real shame."
Butt hurt his ankle in a regular challenge but the same can't be said of goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel.
He is undergoing intensive treatment on an ankle injured in a nasty clash with Arsenal striker Ian Wright.
"It's very swollen but hopefully he'll be all right," said Ferguson.
The keeper was involved in a heated exchange with Wright as the players left the field and Thursday's papers roundly condemned the striker's two-footed challenge.
But there was good news for Ferguson as Andy Cole, starting a league game for the first time this season, showed his best form since joining the club.
The man who has long looked a seven million pounds ($11.3 million) misfit scored the first goal and was a razor-sharp threat all night.
United currently tops the table on 53 points, one ahead of Liverpool with Chelsea sixth on 41 from two fewer games.
Both sides have eyes on other prizes - United in Europe and Chelsea chasing F.A. Cup glory - but their shrewd managers will ensure full concentration on the job in hand.
And another Stamford Bridge full house could be in for a classic encounter.
($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
